name: Tata Steel Ltd
about: Tata Steel Ltd is Asia's first integrated private steel company setup in 1907. [1] The company has presence across the entire value chain of steel manufacturing from mining and processing iron ore and coal to producing and distributing finished products. [2] The company has a target to increase domestic steelmaking capacity to 30 MnTPA by 2025. [3]

sections.one_liner: Tata Steel: India-led global steelmaker. What matters now: FY26 margin gains were cost cuts, and Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell despite guided price rises.
business: Integrated steelmaker with 36 MTPA capacity across India, Netherlands, UK and Thailand, with captive iron ore, coal and ferroalloy mining. [AR FY26]
India is 60% of consolidated revenue. Netherlands, UK and Thailand revenue shares not disclosed. [AR FY26]
India EBITDA Rs34,272cr vs consolidated Rs34,848cr in FY26: India is about 98% of group profit; everything outside India together made about Rs576cr. [Q4FY26 call]
India crude steel 23 MTPA in FY26 (+8%), 74% of group output. Downstream products were over 50% of 9M sales. [Q4FY26 call] [Q3FY26 call]
financial_snapshot: Jun-26 quarter: revenue Rs60,794cr (+14.3% YoY, -3.9% QoQ), EBITDA Rs9,264cr, 15% margin, PAT Rs2,385cr (-19.6% QoQ). [Numbers]
TTM: revenue Rs2.40 lakh cr, EBITDA Rs36,190cr (15.1% margin), PAT Rs11,263cr. Only 31% of EBITDA reaches PAT. [Numbers]
ROCE 12.5%, ROE 11.7%. Both far below the FY22 ROCE peak of 31%. [Numbers]
Rs168 per share: P/E 17.7x, P/B 2.05x, EV/TTM EBITDA about 8.3x, dividend yield 2.38%. Price is 25% below its Rs224 high and near the Rs160 low. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR is -1.6% over 3 years and 8.2% over 5 years (low FY21 base). FY26 revenue of Rs2,32,140cr is still 4.8% below FY22. [Numbers]
FY26 EBITDA Rs34,352cr is up 54% from the FY24 low but only 54% of FY22's Rs63,490cr. Margin is 15% vs a 26% peak. [Numbers]
Quarterly margin rose from 11% (Sep-24) to 16% (Mar-26), then slipped to 15%. The margin upswing may be peaking. [Numbers]
PAT went from a Rs4,910cr loss in FY24 to Rs10,886cr in FY26. Quarterly PAT peaked at Rs3,183cr in Sep-25 and has not regained it since. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings Rs92,382cr in FY26, down only Rs2,419cr despite Rs21,906cr FCF. Borrowings are 2.7x EBITDA; management cited 2.6x leverage at 9M. [Numbers] [Q3FY26 call]
Debt/equity improved from 1.04 to 0.90. Most of that came from net worth rising Rs10,998cr, roughly FY26 PAT, not from repaying debt. [Numbers]
Working-capital days are -56 because suppliers fund operations. But inventory days rose from 171 to 184, against management's working-capital optimisation theme. [Numbers] [Q4FY26 call]
cash_quality: FY26 CFO of Rs35,064cr is 3.2x PAT and 102% of EBITDA. The 3-year CFO/PAT of 8.58x is inflated by the FY24 loss. [Numbers]
FCF went Rs7,868cr → Rs2,569cr → Rs8,731cr → Rs21,906cr. FY26 capex was about Rs13,158cr (CFO minus FCF), close to management's Rs14,000cr. [Numbers] [Q4FY26 call]
Management's FY26 FCF was Rs10,738cr, half the Rs21,906cr in NUMBERS. The small debt reduction suggests the lower figure is closer to the cash actually kept. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: Cost savings of Rs10,868cr exceed the Rs9,054cr EBITDA increase. So price, volume and mix together reduced EBITDA by about Rs1,800cr: the margin gain was self-help. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
Management guided Q1 prices up Rs6,000/t in India and £80/€80 in Europe. Reported Q1 EBITDA fell 5.7% QoQ and margin fell 100bps. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]

Management says capacity expansion is 'circumspect', yet FY27 capex rises 43% to Rs20,000cr. Plus about Rs5,000cr implied dividend, that leaves about Rs10,000cr from FY26-level CFO. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
The global footprint adds little profit: non-India operations, about 40% of revenue, earned about Rs576cr EBITDA, roughly a 1% margin. [AR FY26] [Q4FY26 call]
guidance: FY27 cost transformation savings of about Rs7,100cr, equal to 21% of FY26 EBITDA. [Q4FY26 call]
FY27 capex about Rs20,000cr, more than 60% in India, vs Rs14,000cr in FY26. [Q4FY26 call]
FY27 India volume at least 2Mt above FY26. Ludhiana electric-furnace plant to add 0.8Mt. [Q4FY26 call] [Q1FY26 call]
NINL expansion investment decision in Jul–Sep 2026, first steel around 2029-30. NINL merger into Tata Steel to complete in FY27. [Q4FY26 call]
UK electric-furnace commissioning delayed 6–18 months; management estimates a £150/t cost benefit once running. [Q4FY26 call] [Q2FY26 call]

ledger.promised: India prices +Rs6,000/t, UK +£80/t, Netherlands +€80/t vs Q4. [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Revenue -3.9% QoQ to Rs60,794cr; EBITDA Rs9,829cr → Rs9,264cr (-5.7%); margin 16% → 15%.

ledger.promised: EBITDA better than Q3; volumes about 0.5Mt higher. [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: EBITDA Rs8,200cr → Rs9,829cr (+19.9%); revenue +11.0% QoQ; margin 14% → 16%.

ledger.promised: India realisations -Rs1,500/t QoQ; coking coal +$6/t. [Q2FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Revenue -2.9% QoQ; EBITDA Rs8,897cr → Rs8,200cr (-7.8%). Direction as guided.

ledger.promised: India realisations -Rs2,000/t QoQ; coking coal -$10/t. [Q1FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Revenue +10.4% QoQ; EBITDA +19.8% to Rs8,897cr. Price per tonne not disclosed; result beat the cautious guide.

ledger.promised: Rs11,500cr cost savings over 12–18 months. [Q1FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Rs10,868cr by FY26 (94.5%); NUMBERS EBITDA +Rs9,054cr. Window runs into FY27.

ledger.promised: UK EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY26 exit. [Q1FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: UK segment not in NUMBERS. Feb call said UK 'remains unprofitable'; May call didn't confirm breakeven.

ledger.promised: NINL expansion ready for Board approval by Oct–Nov 2025. [Q1FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Slipped to Jul–Sep 2026; first steel moved from FY2029 to 2029-30. Approval not disclosed.

ledger.promised: +2Mt India volume, Rs7,100cr savings, Rs20,000cr capex. [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Q1 revenue +14.3% YoY, EBITDA +24.7% YoY. Volume and savings not disclosed.

bull: India makes about Rs34,272cr EBITDA at a 24% margin. Another 2Mt of volume plus Rs7,100cr savings could lift group EBITDA meaningfully above FY26's Rs34,352cr. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
At about 8.3x EV/EBITDA and 2.05x book, the price is near its Rs160 low. A Rs6,000/t India price rise would add revenue on 23Mt. [Numbers] [Q4FY26 call]

EU import quotas halving from 30Mt to 15Mt, plus the carbon border tax (CBAM), back management's €100/t Europe upside case. Group is losing almost nothing ex-India, so downside is small. [Q3FY26 call]
bear: Netherlands authorities threaten to revoke coke and gas plant permits, and the UK electric furnace is delayed 6–18 months. Non-India operations made about Rs576cr EBITDA. [Q4FY26 call]
FY26 debt fell just Rs2,419cr on Rs21,906cr FCF. FY27 capex of Rs20,000cr leaves little cash for paying down Rs92,382cr of borrowings. [Numbers] [Q4FY26 call]
Q1 FY27 PAT fell 19.6% QoQ despite guided price hikes. A P/E of 17.7x is high for a 15% margin and 12.5% ROCE. [Numbers]
questions: You guided Q1 prices sharply higher; why did EBITDA fall 5.7% QoQ?
FCF Rs21,906cr in filings, yet debt fell only Rs2,419cr; where did cash go?
Your FCF was Rs10,738cr; what reconciles it to reported CFO minus capex?
Netherlands EBITDA guidance after coke closure, and the cash cost of that closure?

annual_report.business: Global integrated steel producer with 36 MTPA capacity spanning India, Europe, Southeast Asia, and North America. Manufactures flat and long steel products for automotive, construction, packaging, infrastructure sectors. Generates revenue through steel sales, specialty products, and captive mining of iron ore, coal, and ferroalloys.

segments.name: Tata Steel India
segments.comment: Dominant segment, majority capacity, serves domestic infrastructure demand

segments.name: Tata Steel Nederland
segments.comment: High-quality flat products, transitioning to sustainable steelmaking

segments.name: Tata Steel UK
segments.comment: Building EAF-based facility with UK government support

segments.name: Tata Steel Thailand
segments.comment: Reinforcement and infrastructure steel via EAF route

annual_report.revenue_mix: India dominant at 60% of consolidated revenue. Products: flat products, long products (rebars, wire rods). Customers: automotive, construction, packaging, infrastructure, engineering sectors.
strategy: Market leadership through scale, product differentiation, customer engagement
Profitable growth via India capacity expansion (NINL +4.8 MT, Thriveni Pellets)
Global cost leadership through raw material security and supply optimization
ESG industry leadership: Net Zero 2045, low-carbon technologies deployment
Digital transformation acceleration and customer-centric innovation platform
annual_report.outlook: India steel demand growth 7-8% in FY2026-27; Apparent Steel Use reach 176-178 MT. Global demand modest 1.3% recovery in 2026. Infrastructure spending sustained. Headwinds: Chinese excess capacity, trade protectionism, geopolitical tensions.
annual_report.capex_plans: Ludhiana EAF completed (₹3,200 crore). Ongoing: NINL expansion, TSUK EAF construction, TSN decarbonization, HIsarna demo plant, EASyMelt technology implementation.
risks: Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz blockade disrupting energy markets, logistics
Chinese excess capacity and aggressive exports intensifying trade protectionism globally
Energy cost volatility and commodity supply chain disruptions impacting input costs
Regulatory and execution risks for major transformation projects (TSUK, TSN)
